topIssues.title: opgeth-decoupling: migrate op-chain-ops/genesis to build against upstream go-ethereum
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
Part of #20257. See §14 of the [op-geth decoupling doc](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/develop/docs/ai/opgeth-decoupling.md).

## Goal

Make `op-chain-ops/genesis` build OP-Stack L2 genesis against **upstream** go-ethereum, removing its dependency on op-geth's `params.ChainConfig`.

## Background

`BuildL2Genesis` ([genesis.go:49](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/f176635fafcd5e7f6dc07b52e391bdc0c249fda6/op-chain-ops/genesis/genesis.go#L49)) builds a go-ethereum `params.ChainConfig` **literal** from `DeployConfig`, uses its `IsEcotone`/`IsHolocene`/`IsIsthmus`/`IsJovian` to set genesis fields, then puts it in `core.Genesis.Config` → `ToBlock()` (genesis state root) and serialises it into `genesis.json`. This is op-geth **as a library**, and it stays — but it must move to upstream geth, which cannot represent the OP fork fields.

## The one op-geth diff that matters

The only OP-specific behaviour in op-geth's genesis path is in `core/genesis.go`: for **Isthmus+** chains the genesis block's `WithdrawalsHash` is set to the storage root of the `L2ToL1MessagePasser` predeploy (`statedb.GetStorageRoot`, itself an upstream primitive) instead of the empty withdrawals hash (`hashAlloc`/`flushAlloc`/`toBlockWithRoot`). Everything else — alloc → state trie, `statedb.Commit`, Shanghai/Cancun/Prague header fields — is identical upstream code.

## Plan

- `op-chain-ops/genesis` builds an `opparams.ChainConfig` (#20260) and serialises it as the `genesis.json` `config` (it carries the OP fields + tags; upstream's `ChainConfig` cannot).
- Compute the genesis block/state-root against upstream go-ethereum via `(*opparams.ChainConfig).GethChainConfig()` (the Ethereum fork schedule suffices for `ToBlock`).
- Port the ~15-line Isthmus withdrawals-root rule into the monorepo on top of upstream `state`/`triedb` + the `L2ToL1MessagePasser` predeploy address (`op-core/predeploys`).

## Dependencies

- #20260 (`op-core/params` + `GethChainConfig()`).

🤖 *Generated by Claude Code*

topIssues.title: kona-node: SafeDB dashboard panels and metrics
topIssues.author: einar-oplabs
topIssues.body:
Part of #23473. Consumes the metrics emitted by #23478.

## Scope

Make the kona-node safedb visible on the kona-node Grafana dashboard and alertable, so an operator can see a stalled or truncated safedb before dispute-mon does.

Panels (one row, panel titles in the house style, lowercase `side: metric (window)`):

- `safedb: tip l1 block` next to the L1 head, with the lag between them as its own stat.
- `safedb: tip l2 block` next to local-safe, with the lag as a stat.
- `safedb: writes (5m)` and `safedb: write retries (5m)`.
- `safedb: truncations (1h)` split by reason (reset, EL-sync).
- `safedb: tip below resume point` as a stat that goes red when the warning from #23478 has fired since the last restart.

Alerts, routed to `team=protocol`:

- safedb tip L1 lag above a threshold for 15 minutes while derivation is advancing (the database stopped recording).
- any `tip below resume point` event (the gap condition from ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#402).
- write retries non-zero for 5 minutes.

The dashboard JSON and alert rules land in ethereum-optimism/k8s. Reuse the op-node safedb panels if any exist so both nodes read the same way.

## Done

- [ ] Panels exist on the kona-node dashboard and render on the kona-node sequencer devnet (ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#283).
- [ ] The three alerts exist, with runbook links to the recovery runbook from ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#404 once it is written.
- [ ] Thresholds are recorded on this issue with the reasoning.

topIssues.title: kona-safedb,op-node: write once per L1 block and gap detection
topIssues.author: einar-oplabs
topIssues.body:
Part of #23473. Stretch goal; not required for the devnet.

## Scope

Carry the todo parked on #22528 from #23112: write one safedb entry per L1 block once derivation moves past it, instead of one per safe head, and make gaps detectable.

Design it for kona-node and op-node together. Two constraints from #23112:

- queries must see the not-yet-written entry, since `superroot_atTimestamp` expects every block at or below local-safe to be recorded;
- finalized must never be ahead of the database on disk.

Gap detection: today a missing entry is served as an older safe head with no error. Decide whether to record every L1 block (so a hole is observable) or to keep an L1 cursor, and whether the check belongs in the node (ethereum-optimism/protocol-team#407 asks the same of op-node).

## Done

- [ ] Design written up and agreed with the op-node owners.
- [ ] Implemented in kona-node, or explicitly deferred with the reason recorded here.

topIssues.title: op-acceptance-tests: integration tests for kona-node safedb
topIssues.author: einar-oplabs
topIssues.body:
Part of #23473.

## Scope

Prove the integration end to end against kona-node, not just in unit tests.

Acceptance suites:

- Remove `SkipOnKonaNode` from `op-acceptance-tests/tests/safeheaddb_elsync` and run `safeheaddb_clsync` against kona-node. Closes #22265.
- Run `TestExecuteStep_CannonKona` against kona-node. Closes #22279.
- Add an op-node parity check: on a network with one op-node and one kona-node verifier, `checkSafeHeadConsistent` passes with kona-node as the checked node and op-node as the source of truth, and the reverse.

Proofs stack:

- An output-root fault dispute game is played to resolution by an op-challenger whose only rollup node is kona-node.
- op-proposer in super-root mode and op-dispute-mon run against kona-node only.

Soak:

- A kona-node on a devnet runs 24 hours with the flag on and a contiguity check (safedb-scan from infrastructure-services, or an in-tree equivalent) reports no gap. Record restarts during the soak and confirm the history survives them.

## Done

- [ ] Both safeheaddb suites pass against kona-node in CI.
- [ ] `TestExecuteStep_CannonKona` passes against kona-node in CI.
- [ ] Parity test exists and passes.
- [ ] Challenger, proposer and dispute-mon tests against kona-node only exist and pass.
- [ ] Soak result is posted on #23473.

topPRs.title: op-zk-proposer: keep witness collection preimages and log trees on disk
topPRs.author: digorithm
topPRs.body:
Stacked on #23464.

On the table path, the native consolidation run reads the receipts of every block it serves from a log-commitment entry. kona-host keeps those receipts in memory until the collection ends, which under an attack that references many large blocks can reach tens of GB per collection and run the proposer out of memory before it can prove a challenged game.

With the new optional `OP_ZK_PROPOSER_DATA_DIR`, each witness collection keeps its kona-host preimages and the native run's log trees in its own `collection-*` directory, removed when that collection ends. Unset, the proposer behaves as before. Startup removes `collection-*` leftovers, because an `emptyDir` survives a container restart after an OOM kill. Stored log trees are checked against the entry before any opening comes from them, so a bad file fails the collection instead of changing a verdict.

Closes the preimage and log-tree parts of https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/proofs-team/issues/33. Batch proofs on disk are deferred until #23464 and #23468 are combined; the issue lists them as a follow-up.

Known gaps, both rooted in kona-host and left out of this PR:
- `PreimageServer::start` aborts its child tasks without awaiting them, so the RocksDB store can still be open when the collection directory is removed. A flush during removal can leave the directory behind until the next restart.
- A full disk makes kona-host retry hint fetches indefinitely, so collections stall instead of failing. The README asks for an `emptyDir` `sizeLimit`, so the kubelet evicts and restarts the pod.

Reviews run: `rust-code-reviewer`, `kona-sp1-cost-reviewer` (no guest cost change), and a security review (approve). The doc, test, and README findings are fixed; the two gaps above are the remaining should-fix findings.

topPRs.title: kona-sp1: prove below-head interop references with log-commitment batches
topPRs.author: Inphi
topPRs.body:
PR 2 lets the SP1 consolidation check a message to a block below the initiating chain's local safe head against a log-commitment entry instead of that block's receipts. This PR makes the proposer (and the executor test tool) use it, so referencing many large blocks no longer makes one timestamp unprovable.

The proposer scans a game's messages at proof time and picks one path per game: receipts when every request's bound fits, otherwise the table path, where it proves each referenced block once in batches before any consolidation and attaches the covering batch proofs to each request. Requests over the PGU budget, the witness cap, or 4 GiB of stdin are refused, and on the table path the proposer applies these checks to the scan-fixed part of each request before any batch request. `LOG_PATH=receipts` turns the table path off.

The proposer now needs `<vkey>.log.bin.gz` next to the other two artifacts, so prestates published before the log program (`v0.0.1`, `v0.0.2-rc.1`) cannot be loaded. New settings: `LOG_PATH`, `LOG_PROOF_STRATEGY`, `LOG_CYCLE_LIMIT`, `LOG_GAS_LIMIT` (10¹¹).

Testing: unit tests for the scan, path choice, batching, retries, and request checks; ELF-gated tests that pin each estimator at or above measured PGU; interop acceptance with a below-head reference (Kona, SP1 native core, full ELF); a ZK acceptance test on the table path with the mock provider. The pre-check is unit-tested, but no test fails on the baseline at its call site. Gaps: a replaced head's cost is not calibrated (no state in the fixture), executor memory at the caps is not yet measured on Linux, the canary still takes the receipts path (proofs-team#30), and there is no persistent batch cache (proofs-team#31).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

topPRs.title: kona-sp1: check below-head interop messages against log commitments
topPRs.author: Inphi
topPRs.body:
Part 2 of 3. #23361 adds the log-commitment program, this PR checks messages against its proofs in the consolidation, and PR 3 makes the proposer request those proofs.

Today the SP1 consolidation loads every receipt of an initiating block to check one message. For a full 30M-gas block, that is about 72M PGU and 3.7 MB of witness per message, and any log in the expiry window is a valid target. This PR checks a message into a block below the initiating chain's local-safe head against the block's entry from the log-commitment program (#23361) and a Merkle opening. That costs about 0.1M PGU per message, plus an EIP-2935 step for far blocks.

Cannon keeps the receipts path. A block without an entry also keeps it, so the proposer works unchanged until PR 3 requests sub-proofs. The public values, the game, and the contracts do not change. The consolidation stdin gains item 2: deploy the host before or with the new ELF, because an old host with the new ELF halts.

Testing: every `graph.rs` case runs through both paths. The ELF matches native with and without entries. A CPU-proved batch proves a consolidation, and entries that differ from the batch proof do not prove. Replacement rounds are tested at the graph level only.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

topPRs.title: rust: update reth to v2.6.0
topPRs.author: joshklop
topPRs.body:
Moves op-reth onto the reth v2.6.0 dependency stack so it remains aligned with current reth, REVM, and Alloy APIs. The previous fork-only fixes are preserved or superseded upstream, and the Rust/security and reth-update reviews found no unresolved issues.

Migration notes: no flags are removed. `--engine.persistence-threshold` now defaults to 50 instead of 7, `--engine.num-state-masking-blocks` is new and defaults to 30, `--rpc-cache.max-cached-tx-hashes` now defaults to 100000 instead of 30000, and `--rpc-cache.max-headers` is now a hidden no-op; new controls are also available for HTTP compression, inline JWT secrets, and BAL caching.

Verified with the Rust workspace checks, feature combinations, mirror audit, and the affected CL sync, EL sync, and restart acceptance scenarios using both op-node and kona-node.

topPRs.title: op-zk-proposer: bisect proving chunks that exceed witness, stdin or execution limits
topPRs.author: wwared
topPRs.body:
**Draft:** this will change once the related proposer PRs land.

Related: https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/proofs-team/issues/26

When a proving chunk is too large for one SP1 proof request, the op-zk-proposer now splits it by timestamp instead of retrying the same split forever. Before this change, a chunk whose rkyv witness passed the guest's 2 GiB archive limit (for example, blocks of cold `EXTCODESIZE` calls at about 27 KB of witness each), or whose SPN request broke its gas, cycle or memory limit, was resubmitted unchanged on every cycle until the game was lost. The proposer also buffered the whole oversized witness in memory before failing.

What operators see:
- Two new settings:
  - `OP_ZK_PROPOSER_MAX_WITNESS_BYTES` (default 1.25 GiB) caps the witness a multi-timestamp chunk may collect.
  - `OP_ZK_PROPOSER_MAX_STDIN_BYTES` (default 2.5 GiB) caps the encoded stdin of every request, including the child proofs embedded in aggregation stdin.
- A chunk over either limit, or whose request ends `UNEXECUTABLE`, is split in half recursively, down to single timestamps. The log line is `Span exceeds proving limits; bisecting`.
- A single timestamp that cannot fit one request is reported as unprovable. Aggregation stdin over the limit also makes the game unprovable and increments the new `op_zk_proposer_aggregation_stdin_too_large` counter, which needs an alert, because bisection can only add child proofs.
- The guest programs and vkeys are unchanged.

`check_status` now gives a terminal execution status precedence over a terminal fulfillment status. Probes against mainnet SPN showed that SPN executes a request only after a prover is assigned, and reports limit breaches as `UNFULFILLABLE` and `UNEXECUTABLE` together. Under the old order the proposer read every one of them as a retryable `Unfulfillable`. None of the probes was charged.

| Probe | `execute_fail_cause` | `error_trace` |
|---|---|---|
| Gas limit at 1/10 of required | `EXCEEDED_GAS_LIMIT` | `execution gas 1776520 exceeds the request gas limit 177652` |
| Cycle limit at 1/10 of required | `EXCEEDED_CYCLE_LIMIT` | `exceeded cycle limit of 65835` |
| 30 GiB guest memory | unspecified | `executor child killed by memory monitor (measured 24581 MB)` |

One compressed child proof embedded in stdin with its vk measures 1,272,646 bytes on mainnet SPN proofs. The 2.5 GiB default therefore fits about 2,109 child proofs, or about 1,054 spans.

rkyv 0.8 panics, rather than returning an error, when the witness archive overflows its 32-bit offsets. The executor catches that panic and reports it as an oversized witness.

## Known gaps
- **Aggregation stdin is checked only at submission.** The check runs after every child proof has been bought, and that spend is lost when the game is reported unprovable. With 1.27 MB child proofs, the stdin limit binds at about 1,054 spans, which is before the aggregation request's 1e9 PGU limit (about 4,000 spans, estimated). A possible fix is to project the aggregation size in `prove_span` and refuse to split past it.
- **One timestamp's real witness ceiling is below 2 GiB.** A single timestamp may collect up to the 2 GiB archive limit, but SPN kills the executor at about 24 GiB of RSS, which puts the ceiling near 1.8 GiB (estimate from #26). A witness between the two fails on SPN as a sticky `Unexecutable` instead of being reported unprovable. The game is lost either way; only the label differs.

## Review
`rust-code-reviewer`, `kona-sp1-cost-reviewer` and a general review were run, and their findings are fixed except for these:
- **Dismissed: commit 3 rejects some chunks before commit 4 adds bisection.** On its own, commit 3 rejects 1.25–2 GiB chunks that commit 4 then bisects. The PR is squash-merged, so that intermediate state never reaches `develop`.
- **Deferred:** the two known gaps above.

`just lint-clippy` fails on `develop` because of an existing `missing_const_for_fn` in `kona-derive`, which this PR doesn't touch.
